talk: Every buyout ends with an exit: selling to a bigger company (a trade sale), selling to another PE firm (a secondary buyout), or listing shares on a stock market (an IPO). The best route is the one that pays the most, most certainly. A higher price you might get later is worth less than a good price you get today.

terms.meaning: Selling to a company in the same business.
Listing shares on a stock market so the public can buy them.

questions.prompt: A media group offers 10 times EBITDA for the club. EBITDA is $6M. What's the offer?
whyNot: $6M x 11 = $66M is the IPO valuation, not the trade sale.
$80M doesn't come from these numbers. $6M x 10 = $60M.

questions.prompt: In an IPO you'd sell only 30% of the club at first, at 11 times EBITDA. How much cash comes in on day one?
questions.hint: Whole club value, then the 30% you sell.
whyNot: $66M is the whole club's value. You only sell 30% at first.
$60M x 30% = $18M uses the trade sale price.

questions.prompt: The club has $20M of debt. In the trade sale, what do the owners get?
whyNot: $60M + $20M = $80M adds the debt. It comes off.
Lenders get repaid first: $20M comes off.
$66M - $20M = $46M uses the IPO value, but most of that isn't cash yet.

penalty.prompt: In an IPO the club is valued at {m} times EBITDA of {ebitda}. You sell {float} of it on day one. How much cash comes in?
penalty.hint: Whole club value first, then the share you sell.
working: {ebitda} x {m} = {ebitda * m|usd} for the whole club.
{ebitda * m|usd} x {float} = {ebitda * m * float|usd} on day one.

traps.why: That's the whole club. An IPO sells only {float} at first.

call.title: The exit
call.prompt: Season's end. A media group offers 10 times yearly profit for all of your stake, in cash. Or list the club and sell 30% of your stake now at 11 times, keeping the rest. Or hold on for another season.

options.label: Trade sale: sell everything at 10 times
options.result: Good call. A good multiple, all in cash, today. Certain money beats possible money.

options.label: IPO: sell 30% at 11 times
options.result: A higher multiple, but only on 30% now. The rest depends on the stock market later.

options.label: Hold another season
options.result: Holding is a bet that next season beats a 10 times offer in hand.

takeaway: The best exit pays the most, most certainly. Lenders are paid before owners.
